steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Remove pulp and strings from pumpkin seeds. Wash and thoroughly dry seeds.

Place melted butter in a large bowl; add seeds and toss until evenly coated. Transfer seeds to the prepared baking sheet; sprinkle with 2 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon. Stir to coat; spread into a single layer.
Bake in the preheated oven for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle seeds with 2 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon; stir to coat, spread into a single layer, and bake for 5 minutes more.
Sprinkle seeds with 2 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon; stir to coat, spread into a single layer, and bake 5 minutes more.
Sprinkle seeds with remaining 2 tablespoons sugar; stir to coat and spread into a single layer.
Bake until sugar is coated onto seeds, about 10 minutes more. Cool seeds on the baking sheet.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Pumpkin Seeds
raw_recipe.description: For this sweet pumpkin seeds recipe, coat those leftover pumpkin seeds with butter, cinnamon, and sugar for the most satisfying, fiber-filled snack.

review.reviewBody: I put these in the oven while guests were arriving at my son's birthday party. The aroma of cinnamon filled the house and they were a hit with the guests. I had about four cups of pumpkin seeds that were soaking in salt water overnight. I dried them in the oven for about 15 minutes at 350 degrees and then added the sugar and cinnamon and turned them every 10 minutes because of the moisture in the soaked seeds. They were nice and crunchy with a sweet and salty taste. I started eating them and couldn't stop. YUMMY!

This recipe turned out great! I was a little apprehensive when I read some of the previous reviews so I made few a few changes and was very pleased with the results. I substituted homemade pumpkin pie spice instead of straight cinnamon and I baked them each stage for 10 minutes. They were terrific! Like honey roasted peanuts except they were pumpkin seeds! Will definitely make again!

I made two batches of this tonight with our pumpkin seeds from last night's pumpkin carving. I was in a hurry and didn't read the directions very well. Instead of 2T of sugar, I was using 2t sugar each time. They turned out really good. I think maybe using less sugar prevented the "brittle" version that several reviewers complained about. I also used parchment paper on my baking sheet and just slid the seeds back into the bowl to add each round of cinnamon and sugar. Very little mess for a very yummy result.

yummy and perfect. I don't even like pumpkin seeds usually but these are good. I followed the recipe to the letter except I think I used about 2.5 TBS of butter since that is what I had left of one stick. I had no issues with it turning into brittle at the end. as soon as I pulled it out of the oven I stirred it and tapped any clumps with the edge of my spoon so maybe that was the trick. Oh, and per one suggestion I dumped the seeds back into the bowl I used to coat them with butter and Cin/Suger the first time and stirred them in that after each baking cycle so again maybe that help my seeds to stay separate.

YUM! Reminds me of the flavor of Kettle Corn! I didn't use the butter as I didn't want the extra calories and fat. Instead I just sprayed the baking pan with cooking spray. I used only enough sugar and cinnamon to lightly coat them.

I only used about 1 Tablespoon melted butter. I also have a big shaker that has cinnamon and sugar mixed already(we love cinnamon and sugar). So this was really easy to follow. They did come out good, but may have over baked just a little. So, just keep checking them and turning them.

Fabulous recipe...they came out perfect. I used parchment paper, so every time they needed to be mixed with sugar it was easy to pick up the paper and slide the seeds into the bowl. I spread them out as best I could every time and after the last 10 minute bake I didn't think they were quite roasted enough so they went back in for another 5. I did use 3 cups of pumpkin seeds because that's what I had on hand, which may be why I needed a little more cooking time. Anyway they're delicious...roasty, toasty, crunchy and cinnamony!

Have been using this recipe for a couple of years, now. I love it! This year I decided to add a pinch of ground cloves and a pinch of nutmeg to the mix. Talk about Delicious! Its like having a pumpkin pie! Minus most of the fat and calories generally associated with any pie. Always fun to tinker with and experiment around some of my favorite recipes. This is definitely one of them.

Delicious! I just put the ingredients in a big plastic container and shook them around at each interval. Worked like a charm. I also use a silicone sheet on my pan so very easy clean-up without added grease.

Sweet and crunchy. I made it a little less messy and used less dishes by tossing the seeds, butter, cinnamon, and sugar in a freezer bag and then poured right onto a cookie sheet lined with wax paper. (:

These turned out really good! I'm not a huge fan of pumpkin seeds, but wanted my kids to try them and I have to say, I was impressed. They were easy to make and not messy at all... I didn't have parchment so I used aluminum foil and lightly sprayed it with cooking spray. I stirred the seeds and butter in a bowl to coat, then added the cinnamon and sugar (per recipe instructions)... stirred again to coat and baked... at each interval, I put the seeds back in the bowl to mix and recoat. Had to cook an additional 10 min to get the consistency I wanted, but other than that, I didn't change anything :).
I made it for friends, and they loved it. I'm not a fan of pumpkin seeds in general. Very easy to make and bake.
this is a grate chang from rosting pumkinseds for 7 years, I love it!!!!!
Not what I was expecting- more gooey than baked and crunchy.
It got very sticky for me and I have had better tasting sweet seeds. The seeds also didn't cook all the way thru.
This was our first attempt with pumpkin seeds - just found it to be "meh". The cinnamon stuck to the seeds but the sugar - not so much.
Simple, and delicious. I don't like regular, salty pumpkin seeds, but these are addictive. My 3 little kids loved them.
Excellent results. Followed recipe exactly, and I had to send people home with bags of them by request- they were that good!
Followed directions and it burned really fast. I recommend lowering the temp and not doing the last 10 minutes.

My kids loved this recipe. It is a nice change from the usually salty seed recipes. I followed the recipe as directed. Only difference is that I washed and dried my seeds the day before so they were good and dry. There were some seeds that stuck together like brittle, but that didn't seem to bother my son who is devouring them at this moment.
